Question: Let \(\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^d\), with \(d\le 3\), be a smooth bounded open set, and let \(n(x)\) denote the outward unit normal on \(\partial\Omega\). For \(i=1,\dots,4\), fix diffusion coefficients \(d_i>0\) and nonnegative initial data \(a_i^{in}\in C^{\infty}(\overline{\Omega})\) satisfying the compatibility condition for homogeneous Neumann data, namely \(\nabla a_i^{in}\cdot n=0\) on \(\partial\Omega\). Consider the system for the unknowns \(a_i=a_i(t,x)\), \(i=1,\dots,4\),
\[
\partial_t a_i-d_i\Delta a_i = (-1)^i\,(a_1a_3-a_2a_4)
\quad \text{in } (0,\infty)\times\Omega,
\]
together with the boundary conditions \(\nabla a_i\cdot n=0\) on \((0,\infty)\times\partial\Omega\) and the initial conditions \(a_i(0,x)=a_i^{in}(x)\). Which statement is the strongest valid solvability claim in this setting?
Predicted label: 'E'
Predicted text: 'For every such compatible smooth datum, there exists a unique global classical solution \\((a_i)_{i=1}^4\\) on \\(\\mathbb{R}_+\\times\\overline{\\Omega}\\) satisfying the system and the homogeneous Neumann conditions, but the most one can conclude is \\(a_i\\in C^{\\infty}((0,\\infty)\\times\\overline{\\Omega})\\); smoothness on the closed time half-line up to \\(t=0\\) does not follow from the stated hypotheses.'
Correct label: 'C'
Correct text: 'There exists a unique smooth solution \\((a_i)_{i=1}^4\\) with each \\(a_i\\in C^{\\infty}(\\mathbb{R}_+\\times\\overline{\\Omega})\\), where \\(\\mathbb{R}_+=[0,\\infty)\\), defined for all \\(t\\ge 0\\), that satisfies the system, the homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, and the prescribed initial data.'
Exact Match: 0.0
